passages.text: Tunde manages a phone repair shop in Ikeja with four technicians. Customers used to complain that repairs took too long and nobody explained the costs. Tunde introduced a simple paper ticket for every phone: the customer's name, the fault, the agreed price, and the promised day. The ticket is pinned to the phone's bag so anyone can see its state. Each morning the team spends ten minutes moving tickets across a board with three columns: waiting, fixing, and ready. Any ticket older than three days gets a red sticker, and Tunde calls that customer personally. Within two months, complaints dropped sharply and repeat customers doubled. Tunde believes the tickets work because every phone has a visible owner, a visible price, and a visible age.

Ngozi coordinates ten volunteer tutors for weekend classes in Enugu. Attendance was poor because tutors cancelled without notice and students stopped coming. She set two rules. First, any tutor who cannot come must find their own replacement and message the group by Friday evening. Second, every class ends with a five-question quiz, and the scores are posted on the notice board every Monday. Tutors whose students improve three weeks in a row choose their preferred time slot first. After one term, cancellations almost disappeared and average quiz scores rose by a third. Ngozi says the turnaround came from making absence everyone's problem to solve and making progress visible to all.

Kwame delivers bottled water in Accra with a small van. Fuel costs were eating his profit, so he tracked every trip for a month. He found that half his trips carried fewer than ten bottles and that he crossed the same junction five times a day. He redrew his route into two loops, set a minimum order of fifteen bottles for free delivery, and charged a small fee below that. He also calls his regular shops every Sunday evening to confirm Monday orders instead of driving around to ask. Fuel use fell by a third while bottles delivered stayed the same. Kwame credits the logbook: once he measured the waste, the fixes were obvious.
